supporting_sources.quote: Wade Marquette works at Amazon (2025) received a B.S. in Mechanical Engineering (2019) and an M.S. in Mechanical Engineering (2021) from the University of Washington. His graduated with a PhD from the University of Washington's Mechanical Engineering department, where his research focused on robotics for confined space manufacturing in collaboration with the Boeing Advanced Research Center (BARC). During his PhD work, he developed and patented robots while conducting controls research to simplify robot teleoperation. Wade joined Amazon as a Postdoctoral Scientist in early 2025 and became an Amazon Innovation Engineer (2026) in the Worldwide Engineering and Innovation team, where he develops automated material handling equipment and robotic technologies for Amazon's delivery stations.

After that, he worked on hard disk drives for Western Digital Corporation for three years in their servo pattern write group. There he made contributions in spindle control and advanced servo write techniques with two patents pending. He obtained the Ph.D. degree at the University of Washington in Seattle, Washington in 2017, working jointly with Prof. Mark Tuttle. His research interests are in identification and control of heat transfer in composite materials.

proposal.name: Jonathan Realmuto
proposal.quote: Jonathan Realmuto joined the faculty at UC Riverside. He received a B.S. in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Nevada, Las Vegas in 2010. There he conducted research on PV solar tracking and monitoring. He obtained the Ph.D. degree at the University of Washington in Seattle, Washington in 2017, working jointly with Prof. Glenn Klute from the VA Center of Excellence for Limb Loss Prevention and Prosthetic Engineering. Jonathan's research is focused on the development of powered ankle prosthetics.

proposal.name: Mahdi Ashrafi
proposal.quote: Mahdi Ashrafi joined Boeing BR&T. He was a Commercialization Post-Doctoral Fellow at the UW Center for Commercialization (CoMotion). He received his BSc in Mechanical Engineering from Mazandaran University, Iran with emphasis on solid design. He then obtained his Masters degree in Mechanical Engineering from Northeastern University. He obtained the Ph.D. degree at the University of Washington in Seattle, Washington in 2016, working jointly with Prof. Mark Tuttle. His research interests are experimental mechanics, adhesively bonded joints, composite materials, and application of digital image correlation (DIC) in measuring strains and embedded heating in composite repair systems.
